//: Story Phase 3, chapter 11: The Birth of Frog Grog. That night, in the rain. The crew are in the galley round the one sealed barrel of grog (14,8). Three checks (tag grog_check): the captain's rum cabinet (captain's quarters), Doc Fennimore's medicinal brandy and Old Finch's hidden bottle (crew quarters).

p3c3.begin.narrate: Night. The rain comes down on the Queen Anne's Revenge in grey ropes.
It isn't washing anything away. It's just making the smell wet.

p3c3.deck: hale: So it is. The crew's gathered in the galley. All of them, near enough.
hale: They've got the last barrel of grog. The one we sealed before the Gust. It came through without a scratch.
hale[concerned]: They won't open it without you. They say it's tradition. I think they're scared.
hale: Of what's in a barrel, on this ship, today.

p3c3.deck.tutorial: The crew are gathered in the galley. Take the main hatch below.
p3c3.deck.title: Frog Grog

p3c3.gathering: The whole crew is crammed into the galley, dripping, in a tight ring around a single barrel.
It is still sealed. Someone has tied a ribbon round it. Someone else has drawn a skull on the ribbon.
mags[happy]: There he is! Captain! We waited.
mags: Last barrel of grog on the ship. We stoppered it tight before the Gust. Wax on the bung and everything.
brask[happy]: If anything's come through today clean, Captain, it's this.
garrick[delighted]: Hear, hear!
rook[annoyed]: Nobody asked you.
mags: Toasts first. Proper order. Brask.
brask[happy]: To surviving!
wick[happy]: To Squawks! For being brave!
bob[happy]: To fresh air!
bob[sad]: I just miss it, is all.
rook[happy]: To getting rid of Garrick!

p3c3.gathering.say: crew: To getting rid of Garrick!
p3c3.gathering.name: Everyone

p3c3.gathering: garrick[delighted]: To getting rid of—
garrick[offended]: ...Hang on.
mags: Right. Stand back.
A small yellow cloud climbs out of the bung, looks around the galley, and settles on the ceiling.
brask[disgusted]: ...That's the wax. That's just the wax, burning off.
mags[concerned]: I didn't light the wax, Brask.
mags: ...Mugs. Everybody. Captain first. It's tradition.
p3c3.taste: Mags pours. It comes out slow, and the wrong colour, and it has a sort of shimmer to it.
wick[queasy]: It tastes like the air.
jim[disgusted]: It tastes like the SHIP. It tastes like the bilge, if the bilge had gone off.
sully[queasy]: It tastes like licking the treasure room.
brask[disgusted]: It's got a... texture. Grog shouldn't have a texture.
bob[happy]: I sort of like it?
garrick[delighted]: So do I! Oh, that's GOOD. That's got body. That's got real character.
garrick[proud]: Notes of oak. Notes of rain. A little something of mine, in the finish.
mags[angry]: We SEALED it. We waxed the bung. How did it get IN?
garrick[businesslike]: It didn't get in, Mags. It was already here. It's in the wood. It's in the ship. The barrel just... joined in.
rook[annoyed]: Rubbish. It's this one barrel. It'll be a bad seal. The rest of the drink on this ship'll be fine.
garrick[pretend]: Oh, I'm sure you're right, Rook.

p3c3.taste.tutorial: Check the rest of the ship's drink: the rum cabinet in your cabin, Doc Fennimore's medicine cabinet, and whatever Old Finch keeps hidden in the crew quarters.
p3c3.taste.title: Frog Grog

p3c3.check_rum: Your private stock. Three bottles of Madeira, and one of something from a ship that isn't sailing anymore.
You pull the cork on the Madeira. It sighs at you.
The Madeira has gone yellow. The mystery bottle has gone MORE mystery.
The good whiskey you were saving for your birthday has a thin yellow ring round the inside of the glass, like a tide mark.
p3c3.check_brandy: Doc Fennimore's cabinet. Tonics, salts, a jar of leeches, and a jar labelled DO NOT.
The medicinal brandy is at the front. It is labelled MEDICINAL in large, hopeful letters.
It's yellow. So is the tincture of laudanum. So is the ale Doc keeps 'for the nerves'.
The leeches have all moved to the far side of their jar.
The jar labelled DO NOT has, for the first time in its life, been improved.
p3c3.check_hidden: Old Finch's bunk. Everybody knows about the loose plank. Everybody pretends not to.

then: Finch's hidden bottle, back under its plank. Still yellow. Still somehow smug.
else: Under the plank, wrapped in a sock: a bottle of fine red wine, a flask of cooking brandy, and a very small, very old bottle of something Finch has been saving since his wedding.
All yellow. The wine has gone the colour of a sunset seen through a sick man's eyes.
finch[sad]: ...Forty years I've had that bottle, Captain. Forty years.
finch: Never opened it. Was saving it for a special occasion.
finch[disgusted]: Well. It's had one now.

p3c3.naming: The crew are still round the barrel. Nobody has poured a second mug. Nobody has left, either.
mags[concerned]: Well, Captain?
captain[resigned]: All of it.
captain: The rum. The whiskey. Doc's brandy. The wine. The cooking sherry. Finch's wedding bottle.
captain[resigned]: Every drop of drink on this ship has turned.
jim[sad]: The cooking sherry?
captain: Yellow.
brask[disgusted]: The ale in the gun room?
captain: Yellow.
mags[concerned]: My ginger wine? I was going to use it for the pudding.
captain[tender]: I'm sorry, Mags.
rook: Then we buy more. Next port. Fresh barrels. Problem solved.
garrick[businesslike]: I'm afraid not, Rook.
garrick: Bring a fresh barrel aboard, and by the morning it'll have gone the same way. The ship's in the wood now. Any drink that sits in her takes on the house character.
garrick[proud]: The house character is me.
sully[sad]: So we never get a proper drink again?
garrick[delighted]: Sully! You're looking at it all wrong! You haven't lost a drink. You've gained a PRODUCT.
hale[resigned]: A product.
garrick: Exclusive to this vessel! Unavailable in any port! Aged in genuine contaminated oak!
garrick[businesslike]: All it needs is a name.
bob[happy]: Grog?
garrick: Grog is what it WAS, Bob. This has been through something. It needs a name that respects the journey.
brask[disgusted]: It tastes like bathwater. Out of a pond. After a frog's been in it.
garrick[delighted]: ...Frog.
brask[alarmed]: No.
garrick[proud]: Frog Grog.
mags[annoyed]: We're not calling it Frog Grog.
wick[laugh]: Frog Grog.
rook[laugh]: ...Frog Grog. Hah.
mags[annoyed]: Oh, don't. Don't. It'll stick.
brask[annoyed]: Anyone who calls it Frog Grog is swabbing the heads for a week.
garrick[pretend]: Anyone who DOESN'T call it Frog Grog is very welcome to a short demonstration of the production process.
captain[angry]: GARRICK.
captain[angry]: You do NOT have unlimited authority on this ship.
garrick[businesslike]: Understood, Captain. Limited authority.
garrick[smug]: With a demonstration option.
The Grand Stenchmaster raises his mug. Slowly, reluctantly, under very clear duress, so does everyone else.
garrick[proud]: To Frog Grog!
A small, perfect yellow cloud rolls out of Rook's mouth and drifts up to join the one on the ceiling.
rook[alarmed]: ...That came out of ME.
rook[queasy]: That came out of me, Captain. That was MINE.
garrick[delighted]: Oh, well DONE, Rook! Welcome to the industry!
rook[queasy]: I want to go home.
mags: ...I'll put it on the shelf, then. It's all we've got.

p3c3.naming.tutorial: Frog Grog restores some HP, gives brief resistance to fumes, and has one small, random side effect. Mags sells it in the galley. Any rum you were carrying has turned.
p3c3.naming.title: Frog Grog
